title: LIBRA: Memory Bandwidth- and Locality-Aware Parallel Tile Rendering
problem: Tile-Based Rendering GPUs cannot efficiently utilize additional compute units due to limited per-tile workload, and parallel tile rendering causes memory-intensive applications to suffer from increased memory pressure and congestion.
motivation: Efficiently utilizing additional GPU compute units while managing memory bandwidth is critical for achieving higher graphics performance on mobile TBR GPUs.
method: LIBRA proposes parallel tile rendering with a locality-aware scheduler that distributes memory requests across Raster Units to reduce memory congestion. It predicts tile memory pressure using frame-to-frame coherence without degrading cache hit ratios, then schedules tiles to evenly distribute memory requests during frame rendering.
key_novelty: Locality-aware tile scheduling combined with frame-to-frame coherence prediction to manage memory pressure in parallel tile rendering.
contributions: Parallel tile rendering architecture to efficiently utilize additional compute units in TBR GPUs
Locality-aware tile scheduler that evenly distributes memory requests across Raster Units
Frame-to-frame coherence-based memory pressure prediction mechanism
20.9% speedup, 13.5% memory latency reduction, 11.4% throughput improvement, and 9.2% energy savings on commercial gaming applications
primary_theme: Memory-aware tile scheduling for TBR GPUs
